outline: This course develops students’ human-centered GenAI literacy through authentic translation projects on the Global Voices Lingua platform. Students use Custom GPTs and Dify as complementary tools for responsible AI-assisted translation rather than as automatic translation engines. Custom GPTs support translation reasoning by helping students ask questions, identify problems, compare wording options, and reflect on decisions. Dify supports workflow awareness by helping students organize the translation process, follow review checkpoints, record AI support, and document human decisions. Across three project cycles—political and social affairs, science and the environment, and culture and diverse voices—students use and gradually adapt instructor-designed Custom GPTs and a reusable Dify workflow template. By the end of the course, students will be able to use AI tools critically, adapt human-AI translation workflows, and maintain responsibility for final translation decisions.

flexible_learning.content:
1. Week 17: Students watch the instructor-produced guidance video for producing the "Three-Project Translation Quality Review Report." The report focuses on the final translations from three translation projects as its subject of analysis, requiring students to write a quality review report that demonstrates an overall understanding of translation quality judgment criteria and their trajectory of growth.

2. Week 18: Students complete a review report of approximately 1,000 words
flexible_learning.outcome:
1. Week 17: Cross-check and record students' viewing hours in the backend of NTUT's i-School PLUS platform, while simultaneously setting up a discussion board on Zuvio to guide interaction.

2. Week 18: Students submit their review report via the Zuvio platform.
flexible_learning.assessment_ratio: Learning outcomes from the flexible week(s) account for 10% of the total grade.
